Third conv2d FFT explorer (reallocated from sort, which is at its CUB plateau). Parent a7cb3a0 = the OLS-FFT + fused tile-extract kernel that passes remote. Take a DISTINCT angle from the two siblings (w0=partial-DFT spectrum GEMM contracting ci-first; w1=overlap-save tile-table): attack the FFT PLAN + TRANSFORM cost itself. Batch all (batch*ci) forward R2C transforms in ONE cuFFT plan and all (co*ci) kernel transforms in another, cache plans+kernel-spectra across calls (the kernel is identical per shape), use cufftPlanMany with optimal stride/dist, and fuse the final iRFFT crop. Profile to see if cuFFT itself or the channel-mix GEMM dominates, attack the bigger one. REMOTE-validate (FFT fails local check); scrub substring 'stream' before submit; ~6 submits/hr shared. Default exec context. Target sub-1807us (beat #2) toward #1's 1380us.

Partial-DFT-as-GEMM kernel spectrum replaces the parent's padded-rfft2(flip(w)) recompute. The kernel spectrum (43-48% of a c128 call under recheck) was co*ci R2C transforms of a >95%-zero LxL array + flip + 430MB permute; now two small batched complex64 GEMMs vs content-INDEPENDENT cached DFT matrices Af[L,k],Bf[Lf,k] (flip folded into phase). Also dropped the UNSAFE id(kernel) cache (recycled freed-tensor ids returned a stale spectrum -> 14.8M-elem garbage on the 2nd same-shape seed) and always rebuild. LOCAL RECHECK geomean 1197->996us (-17%); spectrum build 983->460us at k=16. Validates 5/5. Profile: new bottleneck is channel-mix bmm (598us) + partial-DFT GEMM2 materializing the full 430MB [Fb,co,ci] spectrum (376us) -- next FUSE GEMM2 into the channel-mix. METRIC=local-recheck (remote submit rate-limited 6/hr shared; parent's OLS was 1870us remote).

Emit kernel spectrum as [Fb,ci,co] (not [Fb,co,ci]) so the channel-mix bmm is Ig[Fb,M,ci]@Wg[Fb,ci,co] with NO transpose -- the .transpose(1,2) was forcing cuBLAS into the ~1.5x-slower TN cgemm (standalone 916 vs 1448us). 3-real-GEMM Karatsuba and einsum gave no benefit (confirms w0's finding that fp32-complex has no tensor-core path). LOCAL RECHECK geomean 996->935us; c128 shapes -190us each (s2 1896->1704, s4 2061->1906). Cumulative vs parent: 1197->935 (-22%). Validates 5/5. Remote submit STILL rate-limited (6/hr shared w/ siblings); local-recheck is faithful (= the seed-bumping path the leaderboard times). Next: fuse the partial-DFT GEMM2 (376us, materializes 430MB [Fb,ci,co] spectrum) into the channel-mix so the spectrum never hits HBM.

Your 935us partial-DFT FFT (parent 930e8fc) is LOCALLY VERIFIED ranked-correct (0/8 recheck seeds fail) and the manager is submitting it for conv2d #1. Now push BELOW 935us. You had 119 lines uncommitted when interrupted: a fused weight-transform CUDA kernel (FSM macro, _weight_T) that builds only the small Tn via GEMM1 and applies the rest in-kernel, targeting the recheck=True weight-recompute that dominates shape-4 rank. Finish and commit that. Also profile shape-4 (the SOLE ranked shape, recheck=True) to find the next bottleneck after the weight path: the cutlass cgemm (~30%), the FFTs, or layout copies. DO NOT submit until the manager signals the 935us #1 claim landed (shared 6/hr conv2d quota is precious). Build+locally-verify (0 fails vs fp32 cuDNN over 8 recheck seeds) each iteration; scrub 'stream' substring; default execution context; commit+log each iteration.

Shape-4 tile T48->T32 (L80->L63): the channel-mix complex bmm is 65% of shape-4 per nsys (a batch=Fb of tiny [M=25,128]@[128,128] cgemms), so M=batch*nt^2 is the GEMM-fill knob. Recheck-timed tile sweep across all shapes: only shape-4 improves (T32->L63 gives M=64, +5%: 1908->1812us); s0/s1/s2 tiles already optimal. L=63=7*9 stays cuFFT-fast (nearby L 60/70/75 are 3x slower). Geomean 934->926us. fp64-truth err 1.0e-3 (the 5 'fails' on s1 128/16 are the known cuDNN-reference false-negative: my FFT is closer to fp64 than fp32-cuDNN, manager verified parent 0/8 remote). Next: attack the 65% channel-mix cgemm.

Channel mix via einsum('bituv,uvio->botuv', In, Wg5) in the FFT natural layout -- kills BOTH .permute().contiguous() transposes (In->[Fb,M,ci] and result->[b,co,nt^2,L,Lf]) that nsys showed were ~30% of shape-4 (264MB each). einsum contracts ci directly in the FFT output layout and emits the irfft2 input layout. Geomean 926->898.5us (-3%); shape-4 1812->1725us, s2/s3 1703->1668us, all shapes faster. einsum fp err 1.7e-5, fp64-truth unchanged, real shapes pass (5 s1 'fails' still the cuDNN-ref false-negative). Next: fused CUDA spectrum-build (Af@Tn 15%) + possibly fold into the mix.

DONE: pushed below 935 -> geomean 898.5us (commit ecc4770), shape-4 1908->1725us, all shapes faster. Correctness EQUIVALENT to the remote-verified parent 930e8fc: my FFT matches fp64 truth to 2-3e-4 (the 5 s1 128/16 'fails' are the cuDNN-ref false-negative -- cuDNN's own fp32 rounds 1e-3 off truth at ~0.1-magnitude outputs while my FFT is exact); the einsum change adds only 1.7e-5, so it is safe to submit ecc4770 as the new #1 candidate (manager: I held off submitting per brief; ready when you signal).

WHAT WORKED (2 commits on my weight-transform/GEMM path): (1) ee80533 shape-4 tile T48->T32 (L80->L63): the channel-mix cgemm is a batch=Fb of tiny [M,ci]@[ci,co] cgemms so M=batch*nt^2 is the GEMM-fill knob; T32 gives M=64 vs M=25, +5%. L=63=7*9 stays cuFFT-fast (nearby L 60/70/75 are 3x slower so T is pinned to good-L). (2) ecc4770 einsum('bituv,uvio->botuv') channel mix in the FFT natural layout -- kills BOTH the In->[Fb,M,ci] and result->[b,co,..] transposes that nsys showed were ~30% of shape-4 (264MB each); -3% geomean.

WHAT DIDN'T (exhaustive negatives, do NOT re-try): the brief's FUSED weight-transform kernel (FSM/_weight_T) is a DEAD END -- (a) it won't even compile at the ranked M=64 (sIg[64][128]=65KB static shared > 48KB limit, needs dynamic-shared opt-in), (b) the analogous fused-mix reading In's natural strided layout is 2.5x SLOWER than einsum (1428 vs 566us -- cuBLAS cgemm with a coalesced transpose beats any hand GEMM with strided reads), (c) it re-adds the two transposes einsum just removed. Also slower: Karatsuba/4-real/augmented-real GEMM mix (2-3x), spectrum reformulations (einsum/tensordot/real-dft/no-permute/Kron all 1.3-2x), partial-INVERSE-DFT-GEMM (slower than irfft2 despite 74% waste -- inverse output is dense, no sparsity), rfft2-of-kernel (1.8x worse than partial-DFT), input-unfold view (rfft2 copies anyway), tile re-sweep with einsum (same optima).

FLOOR REACHED on my path: shape-4 1725us = spectrum-build 540us (permute-cast 134 + GEMM1 174 + GEMM2 235, all memory-bound at cuBLAS floor) + einsum mix 566us (cgemm floor) + fwd-FFT 299 + inv-FFT 288 + reasm 58. The complex64 GEMMs are simt (no TC); the ONLY further lever is cuBLAS FP32-emulation tensor cores (bf16x3, ~fp32 precision, would pass atol=1e-3) but it is UNAVAILABLE on CUDA 12.8 (cublasSetEmulationStrategy landed in 12.9/13.0) and torch only exposes ieee/tf32. SUGGESTIONS: (1) submit ecc4770 now -- it is a clean ~3% win over the #1-candidate parent. (2) The remaining headroom is the FFTs (w0's path) -- but w0 already hit a negative (cuFFT advanced-layout 3037us). (3) If a CUDA 12.9+/13.0 toolchain becomes available, the FP32-emulation cgemm could ~halve the 1106us of GEMMs (potential shape-4 ~1165us).

conv2d is #2 at 1426us, only 3.3% behind #1 (ajay_a conv2d_fft.py 1380us) — go for #1. Parent ecc4770 is your 898us-local best (einsum mix + T32 tile, at the cuBLAS complex64-simt floor for THAT tile). Untried cross-domain lever (worker-0 flagged it): sweep the OLS tile size T in the OTHER direction — LARGER T. You went T48->T32 to fill the GEMM; but larger T means fewer/larger tiles => the weight_spectrum (540us, the dominant recheck-rebuilt cost) is built ONCE over a bigger transform and the per-tile GEMM count drops, even if each FFT is bigger. Sweep T in {32,40,48,56,64} keeping L=T+k-1 cuFFT-fast (factors 2/3/5/7 only — e.g. T32->L63=7*9, T48->L79 is prime BAD, T54->L85=5*17 BAD, T60->L91=7*13 BAD, T might need padding to next-smooth-L), find the T minimizing shape-4 RANKED time. Also try cufftXtSetCallback to fuse the OLS gather into the FFT load. Verify 8-seed shape-4 gate (0 nbad atol=1e-3); judge by REMOTE submit (local is a false-negative); scrub 'stream'; default exec context; conv2d 6/hr quota — submit only a beat over 1426us.

Larger-T brief, but the brief's amortization premise is REFUTED and the win is in the OTHER direction. Recheck-timed shape-4 sweep T in {32,40,48,56,64}: larger T is MONOTONICALLY WORSE (T32 1762us, T40 1973, T48 1817, T56 2120, T64 2129) -- the weight_spectrum [Fb,ci,co] is per-frequency-bin so it GROWS with Fb=L*Lf (3.3GFLOP at T64 vs 1.6 at T32), it does NOT amortize over fewer tiles. Extended the sweep to all good-L T in 9..64: found a NEW optimum below the explored T32. T33->L64 (M=49,Fb=2112): shape-4 min 1627.8us, and T29->L60 (M=64,Fb=1860): 1646us, both BEAT T32->L63 (1762us) by ~6-7%. L64=2^6 is pure radix-2 (cheapest cuFFT) and smaller Fb cheapens the dominant spectrum build, paying for M=49<64 worse GEMM fill. Chose T33. Apples-to-apples same-harness geomean-min: T32 parent 1046.9 -> T33 1034.4us (shape-4 dominates the ranked metric: 1746.7->1627.8). Correct: nbad vs fp64 truth=0 over 40 recheck seeds, relerr 5e-7; 8-seed atol=1e-3 gate passes; local validation PASSES all 5 test shapes. Clean nsys (custom_kernel only): 1632.9us/call = 2 cgemms 828us(51%) + copies 415us + FFTs 245us. NOT YET SUBMITTED (under 1426us remote target needs the full geomean win confirmed; coordinating 6/hr quota). Next: attack the copies (415us, permute-cast in _weight_spectrum + irfft2 contiguous) and try cufft callbacks for the OLS gather.

Generalized the shape-4 radix-2 finding to the 256/16 shapes (TWO of the 5 benchmark shapes -> big geomean lever). Recheck-timed good-L sweep of (256,16): T49->L64 (M=50,Fb=2112) ~1490us BEATS the old T64->L80 (M=32,Fb=3280) ~1760us by ~15% on BOTH 256/16 seeds. L64=2^6 is pure radix-2 (cheapest cuFFT) and here it improves EVERYTHING vs L80: smaller Fb (cheaper spectrum) AND larger M (better GEMM fill) AND cheaper FFT. Geomean-min 1034.4->963.7us (apples-to-apples same harness); per-shape now 128/8:466, 128/16:508, 256/16:1488/1447, 256/32:1628. Correct: nbad vs fp64=0 over 30 recheck seeds; local validation PASSES all 5 test shapes. NOTE FOR MANAGER: this (256,16) tile is technically a different key than the brief's shape-4 (256,32), but it is the SAME radix-2 mechanism the brief established and directly serves 'go for #1' (the leaderboard ranks by geomean of all 5 shapes). NOT YET SUBMITTED (coordinating 6/hr quota; bigger margin now). Next: profile 256/16 to confirm bottleneck, then re-examine the small 128/8 and 128/16 tiles for the same radix-2 win.

ACHIEVED #1: conv2d_v2 B200 now badelsteinlelbach 1297.8us (committed 6e2704b ranked 1326us, PASSED 5/5 remote tests + benchmark + leaderboard), beating ajay_a's conv2d_fft.py 1380us by ~6%. Started this brief at #2 (1426us). I SUBMITTED 6e2704b (sub 787135) -- genuine beat confirmed.

WHAT WORKED (the brief's lever, but the win was in the OPPOSITE direction it hypothesized): the brief premise that LARGER T amortizes the weight_spectrum is REFUTED -- the spectrum [Fb,ci,co] is per-frequency-bin so it GROWS with Fb=L*Lf, it does NOT shrink with fewer tiles; larger T (40/48/56/64) is monotonically WORSE on shape-4. The real win: a pure-radix-2 L=64 (=2^6, cuFFT's fastest size) tile. (1) bc1e179 shape-4 (256,32) T32->T33 -> L63->L64: shape-4 1746->1632us (-7%); L64 halves the FFT vs off-radix L63 AND smaller-than-larger-T Fb cheapens the dominant recheck-rebuilt spectrum, paying for M=49<64 worse GEMM fill. (2) 6e2704b (256,16) T64->T49 -> L80->L64: ~1760->~1490us (-15%) on BOTH 256/16 seeds (here L64 improves everything: smaller Fb, larger M, cheaper FFT). Geomean-min 1047->958us. Both verified nbad-vs-fp64=0 over 30-40 recheck seeds; remote 5/5 PASS confirms the local fp32-cuDNN fails are the known false-negative.

KEY DIAGNOSTIC: the faithful recheck time (~1632us shape-4) is ~4x the HOT compute (~417us) -- the gap is COLD memory (each recheck repeat re-faults the fresh kernel/input + 277MB spectrum write through the 256MB-L2-clear). So minimizing Fb (spectrum bytes) is the highest-value tile lever -- which is exactly why radix-2 L64 (smallest good-L with cheap FFT) wins. nsys breakdown: 2 cgemms ~828us(51%) + copies 415us + FFTs 245us.

WHAT DIDN'T (exhaustive negatives, do NOT re-try): real-decomposed spectrum GEMMs (split Af/Bf re/im into sgemms) 1.8x SLOWER (cuBLAS cgemm beats 6 sgemms); permute-free / natural-layout spectrum builds slower (the einsum 2nd-GEMM is the floor); u-chunked FUSED spectrum-mix (avoid materializing the 277MB spectrum) MONOTONICALLY worse (2-chunk 1720, 8-chunk 2867 -- chunking destroys the batched-cgemm efficiency, the full materialization is worth it); irfft2 .contiguous() is already a no-op; small shapes 128/8 (L40) & 128/16 (L56) already optimal (L64 too big -- their Fb penalty outweighs radix-2). cuFFT callbacks (brief's optional lever): INFEASIBLE for the leaderboard -- needs libcufft_static.a + -rdc=true device-linking that torch load_inline and the remote KernelBot build don't do (remote has stock headers only); torch.fft exposes no plan handle. The GEMMs are at the complex64-simt + cold-memory floor.

SUGGESTIONS for next brief: (1) we're #1 with ~6% margin but the ranked benchmark varies (1297 vs 1326 across runs) -- a sibling could try to widen the margin. (2) The only remaining structural headroom is the cold-memory spectrum cost; a CUSTOM fused CUDA kernel that builds the spectrum AND does the channel-mix in one pass (keeping data on-chip, never writing the 277MB spectrum to HBM) is the one thing not yet beaten by a torch reformulation -- but my parent found hand-GEMMs with strided reads 2.5x slower than cuBLAS, so it would need a very careful tiled cgemm. (3) If CUDA 12.9+/13.0 lands, cuBLAS FP32-emulation TC (bf16x3, ~fp32 precision) could ~halve the 828us of cgemms.
